gems.intro: '''Gems''' are [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]] found as special drops from many [[Special:MyLanguage/Mining|Mining]] activities and used in [[Special:MyLanguage/Trinketry|Trinketry]]. [[Special:MyLanguage/Rough gem (Keyword)|Rough gems]] can be shaped into [[Special:MyLanguage/Cut gem (Keyword)|cut gems]] and then crafted into [[Special:MyLanguage/Ring (Items Slot)|rings]]. Gems can also be found as [[Special:MyLanguage/Fine Items|fine materials]], increasing their value.

collection.intro: Achievements are unlockables within the game. Unlocking achievements will earn {achievementPointsLink}. At certain amounts of achievement points, you can unlock special rewards. Some achievements may also give rewards on their own for unlocking them. Achievements have four difficulty levels: Easy, Normal, Hard, and Extreme. There is no relationship between the card colors and any feature of the achievements; they are purely based on which color matches best with the achievement image.

collection.actionsIntro: After selecting an activity, you complete actions until continuing is no longer possible or you choose something else. Each action is one completion of the activity and can award experience, offer a chance to find a [[Special:MyLanguage/Chests|chest]], or create or transform [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]].
collection.categoriesIntro: Activities fall into three broad categories:
collection.chestEligibility: For activities involving more than one [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]], you can only receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Chests|chests]] for skills that have a level requirement.
collection.craftingOutcome: Where applicable, each skill level above a [[Special:MyLanguage/Recipes|recipe's]] requirement also grants +1 [[Special:MyLanguage/Quality Outcome|crafting outcome]] for the resulting crafted item, with no cap.
collection.equipmentBonuses: Only the primary skill determines which [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] bonuses apply to an activity. Bonuses that apply to the primary skill also affect experience awarded to secondary skills.
collection.finite: '''Finite activities''' — [[Special:MyLanguage/Recipes|recipes]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Travelling|travelling]] generally have a limited number of possible actions. For recipes, you select an amount up to the maximum allowed by your available materials, and the game estimates the required steps. Travelling continues until you reach the destination.
collection.intro: There are many '''activities''' to perform throughout the world of [[Special:MyLanguage/Arenum|Arenum]].
collection.movement: '''[[Special:MyLanguage/Movement Activities|Movement activities]]''' — These move you to another location after one completed action. They include ordinary activities such as {ventureActivityLink}, as well as anti-softlock escape options such as {emergencyActivityLink} for locations you cannot otherwise leave with your current equipment.
collection.nearInfinite: '''Repeatable activities''' — Many gathering activities complete an action after a set number of steps and continue until you choose something else. For example, {activityLink} keeps producing pine logs while it can continue. Activities remain fully efficient until the inventory soft cap is reached, and can optionally stop when you become [[Special:MyLanguage/Overencumbered|overencumbered]].
collection.seoDescription: Activities are the actions a character can perform while walking in WalkScape.
collection.skillsIntro: The following skills have associated activities. Each skill page lists its activities and where they can be performed.
collection.stepHandling: Steps recorded while the game is in the foreground are applied to the current activity in real time. Steps recorded while the game is closed or in the background are applied when you return to it.
collection.workEfficiency: Each level above an activity's skill requirement grants 1.25% [[Special:MyLanguage/Attributes|work efficiency]] for that activity, up to 25% at 20 levels above the requirement.

collections.collectiblesIntro: '''Collectibles''' are special [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] that require no [[Special:MyLanguage/Inventory|inventory]] space and get added automatically once found under your Character icon > Achievements > Special Items > Collectibles. If they have an effect, it will be applied permanently to your character. They cannot be sold or stack once obtained, and you can only have 1 of each. When obtained from an [[Special:MyLanguage/Activities|activity]], they drop from their own table, and thus do not take away other drop opportunities. Each collectible also grants 1 {achievementPointLink} helping you to progress towards rewards and unlocks.
collections.consumablesIntro:
'''Consumables''' are [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] typically made using [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking#recipesSection|recipes]] from the [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking|Cooking]] skill, or obtained from other [[Special:MyLanguage/Activities|activities]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Chests|chests]].

To use a consumable on an [[Special:MyLanguage/Activities|activity]], you must be using enough of it to cover all the steps needed to complete one action.

For example, if one action of [[Special:MyLanguage/Rescue team|Rescue team]] takes you 5,667 steps, you need to use 6 [[Special:MyLanguage/Jelly sandwich|Jelly sandwiches]]. Each covers 1,000 steps, so 6 sandwiches provide 6,000 steps of coverage.

craftedItems.imageCaption: A tool crafting screen, with quality chances shown under the Rewards section.
craftedItems.intro: '''Crafted Items''' are [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] such as tools, weapons, shields, and other [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] made by the player using [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills#artisanSkillsSection|artisan skills]].
craftedItems.qualityDescription:
Each quality includes the base attributes and the bonuses of all preceding qualities. Attributes are predetermined: every [[Special:MyLanguage/Iron pickaxe|Iron pickaxe]] of the same quality has the same attributes.

Your chances of crafting higher quality items increase with skill level, [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]], buffs, and [[Special:MyLanguage/Fine Material|fine materials]].
craftedItems.qualityIntro: Similar to [[Special:MyLanguage/Loot Items|Loot Items]], crafted items come in six increasingly better qualities:
craftedItems.tiersIntro: Crafted quality and material tier interact to produce overlapping usefulness, described by the Gear Score Index (GSI). This chart by floursifter compares qualities and GSI across crafted tiers, using pickaxes and hatchets.
craftedItems.title: Crafted Items

collections.currenciesIntro: '''Currencies''' are used to pay for items and services. [[Special:MyLanguage/Coins|Coins]] are the general currency. The special currency items below are used at particular shops or by the [[Special:MyLanguage/Mysterious Merchant|Mysterious Merchant]]. See each item's page for its sources and uses.

lootItems.intro: '''Loot Items''' are [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] comprised mainly of [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can be bought in [[Special:MyLanguage/Shops|shops]] or obtained from [[Special:MyLanguage/Chests|chests]] and other openables.
lootItems.qualityDescription: Unlike [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafted Items|Crafted Items]], loot items have fixed rarities and attributes. For example, a [[Special:MyLanguage/Shovel axe|Shovel axe]] is always Legendary. Rarity generally indicates an item's power, rather than the number of attributes it has. An Ethereal item might grant a teleport ability as its only bonus.
lootItems.qualityIntro: Similar to [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafted Items|Crafted Items]], they come in six increasingly better rarities:

collections.loreIntro: '''Lore items''' are special [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] that take up no {inventoryLink} space. Once found, they appear under your Character icon > {achievementsLink} > Special Items > Lore items. Any effects apply permanently to your character. Lore items cannot be sold and do not stack, so obtaining another copy provides no additional benefit. All current lore items are delivered in messages from the {mailboxLink}.
collections.materialsIntro: '''Materials''' are resource [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] gathered while training skills and used by [[Special:MyLanguage/Recipes|recipes]] to produce food, tools, weapons, shields, jewelry, and other items. Materials can also be obtained from [[Special:MyLanguage/Chests|chests]]. Materials with a fine version can replace a normal drop at a '''base rate of 1/100'''; fine materials sell for a higher price and improve crafting quality chances.
collections.petEggsIntro:
Pet eggs are [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|items]] that the player gathers from activities or purchases at shops. Pet eggs can be '''claimed''' and then '''hatched''' into [[Special:MyLanguage/Pets|pets]] that can help you on your journeys.

Pet eggs also have a ''Rare'' version that can be received in place of the regular version at a '''base rate of 1/10'''. These can be hatched into rare versions of pets that have a different type and appearance.

keywords.activitiesIntro: These keywords identify types of {activitiesLink}, including those tracked by achievements. They describe the activity itself; equipment required to start an activity is listed under Equipment.
keywords.activityRequirementIntro: An activity may require an equipped item with a particular keyword. For example, {activityLink} requires {pickaxeKeywordLink} equipment.
keywords.bannedIntro: Banned keywords restrict equipment combinations. For example, {sickleLink} and {macheteLink} both carry {foragingKeywordLink}, so they cannot be equipped together. The label does not mean the items are forbidden entirely.
keywords.consumableIntro: These keywords categorize {consumablesLink}, including food, beverages, fishing bait, and memospheres. They may also be checked by achievements.
keywords.containerIntro: These keywords categorize {containersLink} that can be found and opened for rewards.
keywords.currencyIntro: These keywords categorize {currenciesLink}. Weight keywords are listed separately below.
keywords.eggIntro: These keywords categorize {eggsLink}, including how an egg was obtained. A keyword can appear here and in another item section when both types use it.
keywords.equipmentIntro: These keywords categorize {equipmentLink}, including gear and {toolsLink}. They help identify equipment, check activity requirements, and restrict which items can be equipped together.
keywords.intro: Keywords are how the game classifies objects and checks requirements on activities, items, achievements, and more. The lists below group keywords by the objects that use them. A keyword may appear in more than one object section; weight, gear sets, and search keywords have dedicated sections.
keywords.itemSetsIntro: These keywords identify membership in a set of equipment. Set membership can affect attributes, routes, and activity requirements. Diving gear sets, for example, are required for different underwater areas.
keywords.locationsIntro: These keywords categorize {locationsLink} and their environments. They can determine where item attributes apply.
keywords.materialIntro: These keywords categorize {materialsLink}. They can also be used to check achievement requirements.

page.historyRequirement: This keyword is tracked by the progression requirement on {objectLink}.
page.intro: {keywordName} is a keyword used to classify game objects and check requirements. See {overviewLink} for the full keyword overview.
page.restriction: This is a banned keyword: you cannot equip multiple items from its restriction group at the same time. This limits equipment combinations; it does not prohibit using the items.
page.seoDescription: Learn about the {keywordName} keyword, matching objects, equipment restrictions, requirements, abilities, and routes in WalkScape.
page.serviceRequirement: Requires a service of tier {serviceTier} with {keywordLink}.

keywords.recipesIntro: These keywords identify types of {recipesLink}, such as cooking recipes, sandwich recipes, and ore-smelting recipes. They can also be used to track achievements.
keywords.restrictionGroupsIntro: Different keywords can share one restriction group. {fishingRodLink}, {fishingNetLink}, {fishingSpearLink}, and {fishingCageLink} belong to the same group, so items bearing those keywords cannot be equipped together. Restricted keywords below are marked {bannedKeywordLabel}.
keywords.searchIntro: Search-only keywords help filter items by skill, attribute scope, region, or item category. The links below lead to the relevant topic pages; these search keywords do not have individual keyword pages.
keywords.seoDescription: Explore WalkScape keywords by item and object type, including equipment restrictions, weight and stack sizes, gear sets, and search filters.
keywords.servicesIntro: These keywords categorize {servicesLink} used for artisan recipes. {cursedKeywordLink} identifies services with negative effects.
keywords.weightIntro: Weight keywords determine the maximum number of items in one inventory stack. They are shown here from lightest to heaviest.

collection.experience: Pets gain experience towards hatching or leveling up when selected as the active pet or egg and completing an action in an activity that meets the requirements for the pet. Eggs do not have any requirements. Pets gain 1 experience point per step spent on the activity, including steps used from the step bank. For example, completing an activity action that takes 50 steps awards 50 pet experience. Double action, double rewards, and XP attributes do not affect the amount of pet experience earned.
collection.intro: Pets are companions that you can summon to join and aid you on your travels in Arenum. Pets hatch from [[Special:MyLanguage/Pet Eggs|pet eggs]] that can be found by doing some activities or by purchasing them from shops.

collection.intro: '''Recipes''' transform [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]] into refined materials, [[Special:MyLanguage/Consumables|consumables]], equipment, and other items. Recipes may require access to a [[Special:MyLanguage/Services|service]] in addition to their material inputs. Each level above a recipe's skill requirement grants +1 [[Special:MyLanguage/Quality Outcome|Crafting Outcome]] toward [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafted Items|crafted items]], with no cap.

rewardProgress.achievementIntro: '''Achievement Points''' are given for completing {achievementsLink} and obtaining {collectiblesLink}. Different difficulties of achievements award different amounts of achievement points, and each collectible awards one achievement point.
rewardProgress.checkpointLabel: '''Check Point Unlocks''' — These rewards become available at fixed achievement-point checkpoints and remain unlocked.

collection.intro:
Faction Reputation is a measure of your acceptance with each of the major in-game political factions. Currently those include [[Special:MyLanguage/Jarvonia|Jarvonia]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Trellin|Trellin]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Erdwise|Erdwise]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Halfling Rebels|The Halfling Rebels]], and [[Special:MyLanguage/Syrenthia|Syrenthia]]. Faction Reputation is tightly linked to the Jobs and [[Special:MyLanguage/Job Boards|Job Boards]], and provide a lot of rewards for your hard work in the different realms, guilds, and factions around [[Special:MyLanguage/Arenum|Arenum]]! In addition to geographical realms, Guilds are also planned to use this system in the future.

The Faction Reputation system enables you to level up your reputation in the different in-game realms. This currently may grant you some [[Special:MyLanguage/Skill Experience|Skill Experience]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Items|Items]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Cosmetics|Cosmetic]] rewards, or even access to some special [[Special:MyLanguage/Shops|Shops]]. In this future this may include expanded access to services, shop discounts, new routes, buildings, and cosmetic titles.
collection.title: Faction Reputation

rewardProgress.totalProgressLabel: '''Total Progress Unlocks''' — You gain these rewards based on your total achievement progress and can lose access if more achievement points become available.

overview.chestIntro: Each route consists of ten travelling actions, with an independent chance of finding an {chestLink} on each action. The '''Base Chest Chance (Per Action)''' column shows the chance for one action; '''Base Chest Chance (Per Route)''' shows the chance of finding at least one chest over all ten actions. These base chances depend on Base Steps and are unaffected by travelling efficiency or step reduction. They exclude [[Special:MyLanguage/Chest Finding (Mechanics)|Chest finding]] bonuses.
overview.intro: Routes connect two [[Special:MyLanguage/Locations|locations]] on the [https://map.walkscape.app/ game map]. The tables below show unmodified base distances. Your actual travel distance depends on your [[Special:MyLanguage/Agility|Agility]] level and equipment bonuses to [[Special:MyLanguage/Travelling (Mechanics)|travelling]]. Base distances are the same in both directions, but route requirements may differ.

intro.inventory:
The Mysterious Merchant will buy items that come from chests, and give you chest-specific chips in exchange that you can use to buy other chest items.

You don't need to bring what you want to sell with you, the Mysterious Merchant can pull items directly from your bank.
intro.prices: The Mysterious Merchant has a fixed buying and selling price based on the rarity of the item.

pageDesc.mailbox:
The '''Mailbox''' is a [[Special:MyLanguage/Services|service]] that allows players to receive mail and claim attached items.

Mailboxes are available in locations that have a [[Special:MyLanguage/Banks|bank]] available. The Mailbox can also be opened from the inventory, but items may only be claimed while at a full service bank.

The mailbox was introduced as part of the wider development of upcoming trading features, but as of now trading and sending items or mail to other players are not possible. The Mailbox currently provides a way for the developers to send mail, rewards, and other surprises to players, and it is planned to support future systems such as trade deliveries and event rewards.
pageDesc.mysteriousMerchant: The '''Mysterious Merchant''' offers the service of trading chest loot for chest specific chips and then selling chest loot for the ships. There is a 1:4 rate between selling and buying.
pageDesc.skilling: The '''{serviceName}''' is the service needed for most {skillLink} [[Special:MyLanguage/Recipes|recipes]].
pageDesc.wardrobe: The '''Wardrobe''' service allows your character to change or apply different [[Special:MyLanguage/Cosmetics|cosmetics]] you have gained or purchased. Wardrobes are generally available in every city.

intros.agility: The '''Agility''' utility [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to gain experience by travelling between locations. Higher Agility levels give you access to better [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can help you travel faster. Equipment such as [[Special:MyLanguage/Skis (Keyword)|skis]] and the [[Special:MyLanguage/Grappling hook|grappling hook]] can change the number of steps required to cross different types of terrain. Future plans for travelling include random events, small quests, discoveries, and items to collect along the way. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Agility chest|Agility chests]] as rare drops while training Agility.
intros.carpentry: The '''Carpentry''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to process [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]] such as logs into planks. Future plans for the skill include constructing farm buildings. Higher Carpentry levels give you access to more types of logs and [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Carpentry efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Carpentry chest|Carpentry chests]] as rare drops while training Carpentry.
intros.cooking: The '''Cooking''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to prepare [[Special:MyLanguage/Consumables|consumables]] that provide temporary skilling boosts. Some recipes are simple, such as cooking fish, while others require several [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]]. Higher Cooking levels give you access to more ingredients, better recipes, and [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Cooking efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking chest|Cooking chests]] as rare drops while training Cooking.
intros.crafting: The '''Crafting''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to create [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] such as fishing rods, pickaxes, and hatchets for training other skills. Equipment can be crafted in six different [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafted Items#Quality|qualities]], and using [[Special:MyLanguage/Fine Material|fine materials]] increases your chances of making a higher quality item. Higher Crafting levels let you work with more materials to make better items and use equipment that can improve your Crafting efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafting chest|Crafting chests]] as rare drops while training Crafting.
intros.fishing: The '''Fishing''' gathering [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to catch different species of fish. Fish can be cooked with the [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking|Cooking]] skill to turn them into [[Special:MyLanguage/Consumables|consumables]]. Higher Fishing levels give you access to more species of fish and better [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Fishing efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Fishing chest|Fishing chests]] as rare drops while training Fishing.
intros.foraging: The '''Foraging''' gathering [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to gather materials from natural and urban areas. Forests, hills, and plains provide plants and seeds for [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking|Cooking]] and the planned Farming skill, while towns and cities provide materials for [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafting|Crafting]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Smithing|Smithing]]. Higher Foraging levels give you access to more materials and better [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Foraging efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Foraging chest|Foraging chests]] as rare drops while training Foraging.
intros.hunting: The '''Hunting''' gathering [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to gather animal parts from forests, hills, plains, and some cities. These materials are used in [[Special:MyLanguage/Tailoring|Tailoring]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Cooking|Cooking]]. Higher Hunting levels give you access to more materials, better arrows, and [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Hunting efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Hunting chest|Hunting chests]] as rare drops while training Hunting.
intros.mining: The '''Mining''' gathering [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to extract [[Special:MyLanguage/Ore (Keyword)|ores]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Rough gem (Keyword)|rough gems]]. Ores can be processed into bars with the [[Special:MyLanguage/Smithing|Smithing]] skill. Higher Mining levels give you access to more types of ore and better [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Mining efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Mining chest|Mining chests]] as rare drops while training Mining.
intros.smithing: The '''Smithing''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to smelt ores into bars and create combat [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]]. Higher Smithing levels let you work with more types of ore, make better items, and use equipment that can improve your Smithing efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Smithing chest|Smithing chests]] as rare drops while training Smithing.
intros.tailoring: The '''Tailoring''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to create hand, chest, and leg gear. Some recipes are simple, such as making [[Special:MyLanguage/Linen cloth|linen cloth]], while others require several [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]]. Higher Tailoring levels give you access to more materials from [[Special:MyLanguage/Foraging|Foraging]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Hunting|Hunting]], better recipes, and [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Tailoring efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Tailoring chest|Tailoring chests]] as rare drops while training Tailoring.
intros.trinketry: The '''Trinketry''' artisan [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to shape [[Special:MyLanguage/Rough gem (Keyword)|rough gems]] into [[Special:MyLanguage/Cut gem (Keyword)|cut gems]] and create rings and amulets. Higher Trinketry levels give you access to more recipes, let you make better items, and allow you to use [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Trinketry efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Trinketry chest|Trinketry chests]] as rare drops while training Trinketry.
intros.woodcutting: The '''Woodcutting''' gathering [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] allows you to gather logs by chopping trees. Logs can be processed into planks with the [[Special:MyLanguage/Carpentry|Carpentry]] skill. Higher Woodcutting levels give you access to more types of trees, better hatchets, and [[Special:MyLanguage/Equipment|equipment]] that can improve your Woodcutting efficiency. You can also receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Woodcutting chest|Woodcutting chests]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Bird nest|bird nests]] as rare drops while training Woodcutting.

recipes.craftingOutcomeBonus: Each {skillName} level above a [[Special:MyLanguage/Recipes|recipe's]] level requirement grants +1 [[Special:MyLanguage/Quality Outcome|Crafting Outcome]] toward [[Special:MyLanguage/Crafted Items|crafted items]], with no cap.
recipes.introduction: The following recipes require [[Special:MyLanguage/Materials|materials]] and may also require access to a service, usually at a specific location. Each recipe produces one set of outputs by default.
recipes.tableIntroduction: The following activities are eligible to drop {chestLink}.

travelling.chestChance: The chance to receive [[Special:MyLanguage/Agility chest|Agility chests]] while travelling scales with the base number of steps required to reach a location, rather than using the base chance per completed action.
travelling.efficiency: Travelling has no efficiency cap, but each journey between two locations requires at least 100 steps (10 steps per node).
travelling.encumbrance: '''Travelling is unaffected by the penalties from having an [[Special:MyLanguage/Inventory#Overencumbered|overfilled inventory]].'''
travelling.introduction: '''Travelling''' is one of the main ways to gain Agility [[Special:MyLanguage/Skill Experience|experience]] as you move between locations. The experience gained changes as your [[Special:MyLanguage/Skills|skill]] level increases. The base number of steps depends on the distance between locations; see [[Special:MyLanguage/Routes|Routes]] for the available connections. Each journey is divided into 10 action nodes, which you must complete to arrive at your destination.
travelling.mechanicsLink: See [[Special:MyLanguage/Travelling (Mechanics)|Travelling (Mechanics)]] for more information on experience, chest, and efficiency calculations.
